key_insight: A novel marker-less multi-camera capture system enables accurate 3D reconstruction of hands and manipulated objects in unconstrained, real-world (egocentric) settings, closing the gap between studio datasets and in-the-wild scenarios.
problem_solved: Existing hand–object interaction datasets are captured in controlled studio conditions, limiting environmental diversity and causing models to fail to generalize to real-world egocentric manipulation; this work provides a way to collect high-quality 3D hand+object data outside the lab.
method: Marker-less, multi-camera capture rig designed for near-unconstrained mobility to record egocentric manipulation in diverse real-world scenes.
Multi-view 3D reconstruction and temporal tracking pipeline to recover accurate hand and object poses without markers.
Automated annotation/validation pipeline to produce a large-scale in-the-wild dataset of synchronized RGB and 3D hand+object poses for training and evaluation.
impact: Provides practitioners with realistic 3D hand+object data that improves robustness and generalization of egocentric perception and manipulation models; useful for training, benchmarking, and downstream HCI/robotics applications.
visual_elements: Illustration of the wearable/multi-camera capture setup (top-down and side views).
Side-by-side comparison: studio-captured vs. in-the-wild examples with reconstructed 3D hand+object overlays.
Flow diagram of the capture → multi-view reconstruction → annotation pipeline.
Quantitative bar chart showing improved cross-domain generalization (studio-trained vs. SHOW3D-trained) on a benchmark task.
paper_title: SHOW3D: Capturing Scenes of 3D Hands and Objects in the Wild
paper_authors: Patrick Rim, Kevin Harris, Braden Copple, Shangchen Han, Xu Xie
